_comment: Project-scoped Claude Code settings. Tracked in the plant's own repository, the team shares one hook set: graft makes the baseline commit that records it when the plant has none, and a plant that ignores .claude/ keeps it untracked, so each clone re-runs install.sh to wire its hooks. Per-user overrides go in .claude/settings.local.json (gitignored). Claude Code discovers .claude/agents/, .claude/skills/, .claude/commands/ and CLAUDE.md by fixed convention, and the schema this file pins has no keys for them.
_hooks_comment: UserPromptSubmit runs route-hook.py on every prompt and injects its output (hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext) so the route-first step happens deterministically. Both Claude Code and VS Code Copilot (Agent Hooks, Preview) read this .claude/settings.json hooks block. Path: Claude Code sets $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR to the repo root even when the session cwd is a subdirectory, so use it; Copilot falls back to $PWD (its hook cwd is the workspace root). The interpreter is the Python install.sh found at the seed's floor: `python3` when it is at the floor, else the python3.<n> it wrote in its place. '|| true' keeps it fail-open: a context hook always lets the prompt through. A script that is not there prints one 'cypress: hook script missing' line instead of nothing, and `install.sh --check` runs each context hook once (SPEC-0003, SPEC-0001).
_outputStyle_comment: The main session is no subagent, so .claude/agents/00-orchestrator.md never reaches it. install.sh places the orchestrator's charter and its always_loads as .claude/output-styles/orchestrator.md; keep-coding-instructions keeps Claude Code's own prompt, and CLAUDE.md still loads.

hooks.command: f="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}/.claude/route-hook.py"; if [ -f "$f" ]; then python3 -S "$f" || true; else echo "cypress: hook script missing: $f; continuing without it. Re-run install.sh to restore it."; fi

f="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}/.claude/status-hook.py"; if [ -f "$f" ]; then python3 -S "$f" || true; else echo "cypress: hook script missing: $f; continuing without it. Re-run install.sh to restore it."; fi

f="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}/.claude/bound-hook.py"; if [ -f "$f" ]; then python3 -S "$f"; else printf '%s\n' "cypress: hook script missing: $f; the guard is off. Re-run install.sh to restore it." >&2; fi

f="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}/.claude/resume-hook.py"; if [ -f "$f" ]; then python3 -S "$f"; else printf '%s\n' "cypress: hook script missing: $f; the guard is off. Re-run install.sh to restore it." >&2; fi

_bound_hook_comment: PreToolUse runs bound-hook.py before every Bash call and refuses (exit 2) a blocking-prone command — service control, process signalling, package managers, installers, builds, log followers — that carries neither an explicit bound nor a detached launch. It is a guard, wired without '|| true' on purpose so exit 2 blocks; an existence test around the command lets a missing script allow the call with one stderr line, and install.sh --check names it. Its exit-code contract is in integrations/claude-code/README.md (Hooks).
_status_hook_comment: SessionStart runs status-hook.py once per session and injects `status-register.py --summary` (open / hotfix / deferred counts and the oldest items) so lifecycle debt is in front of the model before it plans. Not per prompt: the register is a frontmatter scan, and a session sees it once. Fail-open like route-hook, with the same missing-script line.
_resume_hook_comment: PreToolUse runs resume-hook.py before every SendMessage and refuses (exit 2) a message to a worker idle past its configured worker prompt-cache lifetime unless its first line starts `continuation:` (delegation.continuation). A guard like bound-hook.py, wired without '|| true' and behind the same existence test; every failure path inside it allows.
